name: Helmut Kohl
summary: Christian Democratic chancellor who led a centre-right coalition: social market economy with some privatisation, firm Western alliance and NATO missile deployment, nuclear power, conscription, and a restricted right of asylum. He drove German reunification and, with it, European integration through Maastricht and the euro with an independent, stability-bound central bank.

abortion-legal.rationale: He pledged a counselling law that puts protection of unborn life first and promised to reduce the number of abortions.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: He said integration does not mean losing one's own identity.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He pledged to reduce federal net borrowing (below DM 40bn in 1983, "zurückführen" in 1989), but the pledges alone are weak evidence.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Kohl said Germany had pushed through the independence of the future ECB from political directives.

class-collaboration.rationale: He appealed to the unions' sense of responsibility, saying that without a basic consensus of the social groups the future tasks cannot be met, and he invited business and unions to joint talks.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He said the government respects Tarifautonomie without reservation, leaving wage setting to unions and employers.

common-currency.rationale: His government negotiated and secured ratification of the Maastricht Treaty with its monetary union.

conscription.rationale: Kohl said general conscription is indispensable for defence.

decide-locally.rationale: He called for applying the subsidiarity principle to EU competences.

defeat-communism.rationale: He pledged to continue economic relations with East bloc states and the Helsinki process.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He backed the forces enforcing UN resolutions on Kuwait against Iraq and expected Germany to meet its UN duties.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He held to firm integration in the Atlantic Alliance and the EU.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Kohl said Germany cannot give up nuclear power (1982), that it remains responsible (1987), and that building new plants must stay possible (1994).

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He defended the Maastricht stability criteria, headed by budget discipline, as binding conditions for joining the monetary union.

free-trade.rationale: Kohl called for free exchange and not protectionism and stressed the importance of the GATT round.

limit-growth.rationale: He said economic growth and environmental protection are not opposites.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Kohl said further privatisation of public holdings would strengthen market and competition, and that more private initiative is a pillar of the social market economy.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: In 1994 he said Germany would in principle take part in measures of the international community to keep peace.

more-religion-public.rationale: He thanked the churches and religious communities and said they can strengthen awareness of values.

national-self-determination.rationale: He said the government is for the right of self-determination of all peoples.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: In 1982 his government pledged to carry out the NATO double-track decision, including deployment if negotiations failed, while aiming at the zero option.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: His government secured ratification of Maastricht, creating the EU with monetary union and common foreign policy.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Kohl listed protecting monuments, movable cultural property and cultivating the common heritage of the nation as policy.

price-stability-first.rationale: He said the ECB was committed first of all to monetary stability and stressed German sensitivity on inflation.

public-ownership.rationale: His government announced further privatisation of public holdings in 1987.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His coalition restricted the right of asylum in 1993; in 1982 he said unlimited and uncontrolled immigration must be prevented.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: German unification took place in 1990 under his chancellorship.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He said his government would work for partnership with the Third World against poverty and hunger.

social-market-economy.rationale: Kohl repeatedly named the social market economy as his programme and said it proves itself in giving social support while modernising.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He held to firm integration in the Atlantic Alliance.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He set "free exchange, not protectionism" as policy.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: Art. 16a(2) bars asylum claims by people entering from safe third countries; the statement goes beyond asylum.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Kohl said social-assistance recipients who can be offered work should get it, and that those who refuse should see their benefit cut.

workplace-democracy.rationale: He said his government would keep the Montan co-determination (worker seats on supervisory boards in coal and steel) and improve its electoral procedure.

notes: Themes searched: economy and welfare (privatisation, Tarifautonomie, social assistance, deficits), Europe (Maastricht, EMU, ECB, subsidiarity), security (NATO, conscription, missiles, Gulf War, UN, Bundeswehr missions), immigration and asylum, nuclear power and environment, life protection, culture, German unity. Evidence is mainly Kohl's own government statements in the Bundestag plus the asylum amendment and Maastricht ratification. Positions on abortion law 1992/95, the Pershing deployment, the Two-plus-Four and Polish border treaties and the CDU donations affair stay null: no record was opened. Government and liberty themes are thin.
